sections.sourcing: No new country shifts, nearshoring moves or supplier renegotiations were reported this week. The standing picture is unchanged: China remains the largest base, with India, Bangladesh and Turkey next, and all clothing, textile and footwear suppliers are now onboarded to Primark's traceability programme. BGMEA's recent push for Primark to source more higher-value product from Bangladesh (and help fund the new minimum wage through pricing) is still open.
sections.strategy: International expansion was the main news this week. Primark opened its first Bahrain store on 23 September (43,000 sq ft at City Centre Bahrain, run by franchise partner Alshaya, its 20th market), and its 48th US store at Augusta Mall, Georgia, on 24 September. Qatar (Doha Festival City, 29 October) and Saudi Arabia (March 2027) come next. In the background: UK home delivery is still being set up, the ABF demerger is targeted for December 2027, and new Chief Commercial Officer Filip Ekvall (formerly of H&M) started on 1 September under CEO Eoin Tonge.
sections.pricing: The 'Iconic Value' price cuts (up to 29% on hundreds of lines, e.g. jeans at £9 and hoodies from £9) run throughout AW26 and are backed by marketing. Competition in the value segment is getting tougher: Inditex's Lefties now has a UK store in Liverpool, with Newcastle and Essex to follow, and trade press says Primark has narrowed its price gap with Shein.
sections.launches: Primark Form, a performance activewear sub-brand launched in the UK on 8 September, is still being pushed with a campaign in gyms and along marathon routes. Its AW collection covers womenswear, menswear and kidswear, split into four lines: Smooth Support, Buttery Soft, Running (shower-resistant, reflective) and Seam Free. The 'By Coleen' AW26 range and the Rita Ora capsule are still rolling out. No new tie-up was announced this week.
sections.gossip: Analysts are still split on home delivery. AJ Bell calls it necessary, while others see it as a defensive move against Lefties and Shein that could eat into Primark's roughly 10% operating margin through fulfilment costs. Investors are wary after the 10 September update (Q4 like-for-like sales down about 3%, Continental Europe down 4.3%, US up 11%), with some calling the digital pivot a reaction to weaker trading.
soWhat: Primark Form points to more demand for technical knits: four-way-stretch, moisture-wicking, brushed 'buttery' jersey and seamless fabrics. Suppliers with that capability and competitive pricing should pitch now for SS27 and AW27 activewear.

Iconic Value prices are permanent and Lefties is now in the UK, so expect steady FOB pressure. Offer cost-engineering ideas (fabric weight, trim simplification, yield) up front rather than waiting to be asked to cut price.

Volume growth is coming from the US and the Middle East (Qatar, then Saudi Arabia in 2027), and UK home delivery will need e-commerce-ready packaging and labelling. Suppliers that can handle flexible, multi-market shipments are best placed for extra orders.
